security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel KVM (arch/riscv/kvm) or trap entry path (arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S, traps.c), kernel writes a value to a WARL CSR (hedeleg, hideleg, hvip, hip, hie, hgeie, vsip, vsie, vstvec, stvec, sip, sie, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus) and relies on the written value having taken effect without an explicit read-back verification, causing the kernel to operate under an incorrect assumption about the hardware CSR state when hardware silently altered the written value on an implementation where the field is not fully writable.
security_spec.summary: Newly formalized WARL rules for hypervisor delegation, interrupt, and trap-vector CSRs mean the kernel must read-back after CSR writes to verify accepted values; failing to do so risks silent misconfiguration of trap delegation (hedeleg/hideleg) causing guest exceptions to route to the wrong privilege level, breaking VM isolation.
